title: Case: A handset is missing from a carton the recipient collected from a pickup point
context: DL-941 is a Tallowmere Goods order of a handset with bundled earbuds. It was diverted to the Larch Street pickup point and collected by the recipient the same day.
initial_request: Please. The carrier chat told me it is delivered and they cannot do anything and then closed the chat on me. That phone was all my savings, I have been putting money away since last summer for it and I don't have it again for another one. The shop man says it came to him open. The driver never even rang my bell. Somebody took it and everyone says not us. Can you just get them to give me my phone or my money back. I can send the photos.

events.body: DL-941 (TG-941, one carton: handset plus bundled earbuds). Route note 16 March 13:22: 'no access, diverted to pickup point'. No door-attempt scan at the flat is recorded. Scanned in at Larch Street pickup point 13:41, driver handover note 'sealed, good condition'. Collected 17:52 against the recipient's collection code. Status Delivered. Depot weight on departure 0.74 kg. Nothing was weighed after that.

I was in all day yesterday nobody came to my flat. I collected the box from the shop and one side was open, the tape was cut. Only the earbuds inside. No phone. I took photos of it on the shop counter before I left because it looked wrong.
The recipient of DL-941 reports the carton was open along one side at collection and the handset was missing. Who reviews this?

DL-941 was collected with the correct code and shows Delivered. There's nothing further tracking can do with a collected parcel. Anything about contents at handover is a Delivery investigations matter. They take it by email with both handover records and any photos. We don't refer cases on for partner desks.

Re DL-941. Our intake log for 16 March 13:41, entered by me: 'tape lifted along one long side, flap loose, accepted as presented'. We don't open or reseal parcels. Handed to the customer 17:52 exactly as it came in. She took pictures at the counter. Hal, Larch Street.

TG-941. We packed and photographed a handset and earbuds in this carton, packed weight 0.74 kg. We can't consider a replacement or refund while the carrier's record says delivered complete. We need the carrier's investigation finding on where the contents went. Not before.

Please. The carrier chat told me it is delivered and they cannot do anything and then closed the chat on me. That phone was all my savings, I have been putting money away since last summer for it and I don't have it again for another one. The shop man says it came to him open. The driver never even rang my bell. Somebody took it and everyone says not us. Can you just get them to give me my phone or my money back. I can send the photos.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask for an investigation of DL-941's contents and custody, setting out the driver's 'sealed' note against the pickup point's 'tape lifted' intake log and the recipient's report.

must: Sets out the conflict without resolving it: the driver's handover note 'sealed, good condition' against the pickup point's intake log of the same minute, 'tape lifted along one long side, flap loose', and the recipient's report that only the earbuds were inside
Asks Delivery investigations to establish where the handset left the carton, including the diversion made with no door attempt recorded, and says photos are available from the recipient

Tells the team why this is pressing for the recipient, using only what the events show (for example that the handset was bought with her savings, that the carrier's chat turned her away as 'delivered', or that Tallowmere will not consider a remedy until the investigation reports), so they can prioritise
must_not: Treats the case as closed, or tells anyone it is, because the parcel was collected and shows Delivered
States or implies that the pickup-point staff or the driver took the handset
Promises or implies a refund or a replacement handset
Sends the recipient a reply that only repeats that tracking shows delivered or that Tallowmere cannot act until the carrier reports
expected.reference_message: Please open an investigation on DL-941 (TG-941, handset with bundled earbuds, Tallowmere packed weight 0.74 kg, same as depot departure weight). The records conflict. Route note 16 March 13:22 says 'no access, diverted to pickup point', with no door-attempt scan at the flat; the recipient says she was in all day. Driver handover note at Larch Street 13:41 says 'sealed, good condition'. The pickup point's own intake log for 13:41 says 'tape lifted along one long side, flap loose, accepted as presented'. The recipient collected at 17:52 with the correct code and reports the carton open on one side with only the earbuds inside; she photographed it at the counter and can send the photos. I am not suggesting where the handset left the carton; that is what needs establishing. Tallowmere will not consider a remedy without your finding. Please note she has told us the handset was bought with her savings and that the carrier chat closed on her with 'delivered, nothing we can do', so an early reference and first update time would matter a great deal. What do you need from her or from the pickup point?

rationale: The driver's note and the pickup point's intake log contradict each other on the carton's condition at the same minute, and nobody has shown where the handset went. Tracking support has said contents at handover belong to Delivery investigations and Tallowmere will not move without their finding, so that is the one team that can settle it. Closing on the collected scan or pointing at the shop would both be picking a side on no evidence.

review.note: Coordinator sent the handover-record conflict to Delivery investigations by Email as keyed; the prioritisation must named two exact details and was rewritten so any true account of her position meets it.
